title: The greatest commandment (Mark 12:28–34)
hookLine: love God with all you are, and your neighbor as yourself

lines: A REAL QUESTION, NOT A TRAP.
cards: After a string of traps, a different kind of person walks up. A scribe, an expert in the Law, has been listening at the edge of the crowd, and he's noticed that Jesus answered well.
So he asks a real question, not a trick. In the King James Bible: "Which is the first commandment of all?" The Law of Moses is long, and full of commands.
If you had to put a whole life's faith on one index card, what would go on it? Jesus doesn't need to think about it. He starts with a single word, straight from the book of Deuteronomy.

teach.b: Here's his answer: "The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment."
It's the first word of Deuteronomy chapter six, verse four, and the name of the prayer built around it.
Deuteronomy itself says to talk of these words when you lie down and when you rise up, and to write them on the doorposts of your house.
Jesus was a Jew, and asked for the heart of it all, he answers from his own people's scripture. He doesn't stop at one. He adds a second, from Leviticus: "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."
Two loves, side by side: love of God, and love of the person next to you. Then something rare in a chapter full of traps.
The scribe agrees, warmly. Well said, teacher. Loving God and neighbor matters more than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices.

teach.h: THOU ART NOT FAR FROM THE KINGDOM OF GOD.
teach.b: And Jesus, seeing he answered wisely, says: "Thou art not far from the kingdom of God." After that, Mark says, nobody dared ask him anything more. One small detail: in Hebrew, Deuteronomy lists heart, soul and strength.
Mark's version has four, adding mind. All of you, every part, nothing held back.

how: Many Christians memorize the two great commandments, and some churches read them aloud in worship as a summary of the Law; in Jewish prayer the Shema is said morning and evening, and Christians sometimes note that Jesus answered from it.

o: Hebrew for hear, the first word of Israel's prayer
Hebrew for peace, a greeting at the temple gate
Hebrew for one, the oneness of God in prayer

games.q: what's inside the passage — tap the pairs.
p: love God with all you are

s: the scribe was trying to trap Jesus
he asked a real question, and they ended up agreeing.
Jesus quoted a prayer Jews still say daily
the Shema, from Deuteronomy 6: talk of these words when you lie down and when you rise up.
Mark lists four ways to love God: heart, soul, mind, strength
the Hebrew of Deuteronomy has three; Mark adds mind.

games.q: a friendly scribe asks you: which is the first commandment of all? what do you answer?
o: Hear, O Israel, and love God with all you are.
love your neighbor, and that's all.
games.why: he begins with the Shema, and adds a second: love thy neighbour as thyself. the scribe agrees, and hears: thou art not far from the kingdom of God.

practice: Say both commandments slowly, aloud or in your head, one phrase per breath: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord; love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, with all your strength; and love your neighbor as yourself.
Then sit with whichever phrase caught you. If you don't pray, you can simply notice which of the two loves feels harder today.

wordCard.voice: Shema. Hebrew for hear, the first word of the prayer Jesus named as the first commandment of all.

orig.note: Hebrew: hear, listen. the first word of Deuteronomy 6:4 and the name of the prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: not far from the kingdom. Two loves, one answer. Tomorrow, a widow at the treasury.
